text:
[NDLC.1.4] Three dialects are built in: `base`, `default` and `realtime`
([LDIA.9]). Running the compiler without a dialect file gives those three.
`realtime` is deferred in this edition, and the compiler refuses a program
that names it ([LDIA.3.2.3]).
Integrators define their own dialects when a tier genuinely lacks a
capability, or when they want the compiler to enforce architectural
boundaries.
